audit.primary_source_citation: Whettlock EM, Woon EV, Cuff AO, Browne B, Johnson MR, Male V. "Dynamic Changes in Uterine NK Cell Subset Frequency and Function Over the Menstrual Cycle and Pregnancy." Front Immunol 2022;13:880438. PMID 35784314 / PMC9245422 / doi:10.3389/fimmu.2022.880438. UPSTREAM LABEL SOURCES (both read): Garcia-Alonso L et al., Nat Genet 2021;53:1698-1711, PMID 34857954 / PMC8648563 (source of the uNK1/2/3 names in NON-PREGNANT endometrium); Vento-Tormo R et al., Nature 2018;563:347-353, PMID 30429548 (source of the dNK1/2/3 definition in first-trimester decidua). Hint check: Wang W et al. Nat Med 2020 (PMID 32929266) EXISTS but is a misattribution for this claim - it profiles seven endometrial cell types (epithelial/stromal/ciliated) and does not define uNK1/2/3; Garcia-Alonso 2021 is the correct endometrial citation, as confirmed by fetching Whettlock's reference list (its ref 28).
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Primary source full text obtained and archived (/home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9245422.txt), as were Garcia-Alonso 2021 (S2_PMC8648563.txt), HECA/Mareckova 2024 (S2_PMC11387200.txt), Guo 2024 (S2_PMC10985329.txt) and Woon 2022 (S2_PMC9880428.txt). NOT obtainable: Vento-Tormo 2018 Nature (PMC7612850 is an EMS record that returns abstract only, so the original dNK1/2/3 clustering methods were NOT read); Strunz 2021 Sci Immunol (science.org returned HTTP 403); Strunz 2026 Sci Transl Med (abstract only); Greene 2025 bioRxiv (biorxiv 403; PMC12265685 blocked by author license). Those four were assessed from abstracts plus reference-list detail only and are flagged as such rather than paraphrased as if the methods had been read.
audit.species: Homo sapiens (human). Counter-evidence includes Mus musculus (Chiossone/Vacca 2014 adoptive transfer) and humanised mice (Strunz 2021).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in four separately-collected public scRNA-seq datasets spanning non-pregnant endometrium (proliferative and secretory phase) and first/second/third-trimester decidua, Seurat anchor-based integration followed by FindConservedMarkers cluster assignment was used to place cells from all stages into three shared clusters, which were then given the names uNK1/uNK2/uNK3 by reference to the pre-existing "annotation" metadata column of the first-trimester decidual dataset; in parallel, in freshly isolated ex vivo lymphocytes, flow-cytometric frequency of CD49a+ CD39/CD103 gates (uNK1 = CD39+CD103-, uNK2 = CD39-CD103-, uNK3 = CD103+), surface KIR2DL1/S1, KIR2DL2/3, LILRB1 and CD94, and CD107a degranulation plus intracellular TNFa/IFNg/IL-8/GM-CSF after 4-6 h PMA+ionomycin, were measured at seven cross-sectional reproductive-cycle stages. NO cell was tracked from endometrium into decidua: no donor contributed both a non-pregnant and a pregnant sample, and no lineage label (barcode, allele, dye, transfer) linked any endometrial cell to any decidual cell. Timepoints are donor cohorts, not repeated measures on the same tissue.
audit.n: scRNA-seq arm (the arm that actually carries the endometrium-to-decidua correspondence): 6 non-pregnant endometrium donors (3 proliferative + 3 secretory, reanalysed from Garcia-Alonso 2021) vs 5 first-trimester decidua donors (E-MTAB-6701, after 1 donor was discarded for clustering independently), plus 1 second-trimester (a pathological accreta case) and 3 third-trimester donors. Flow arm (new data): 29 endometrial biopsies (8 menstrual, 7 proliferative, 10 secretory), 4 postpartum, 10 first-trimester decidua, 16 third-trimester elective caesarean, plus 9 early-labour and 9 vaginal-birth samples; matched peripheral blood from all. Overlap between non-pregnant and pregnant groups = 0 donors. Upstream sources: Garcia-Alonso 2021 = 3 live-donor biopsies + 6 deceased-donor whole uteri.
audit.n_unit: donors (individual women); NOT cells. Cell counts (2,180 endometrial, 18,243 first-trimester, 3,900 second-trimester, 6,077 third-trimester) are pseudoreplicates within these donors.
audit.controls: Present: matched peripheral blood CD56bright/CD56dim NK from every donor (used to show pNK frequency and receptor expression do NOT vary across the cycle, so the uNK changes are not a blood artefact); CD49a (+/-CD9) tissue-residency gating to exclude contaminating pNK, with an explicit check that CD49a+CD9- and CD49a+CD9+ term cells are phenotypically identical; paired unstimulated vs PMA/ionomycin wells; fresh-vs-rested stimulation optimisation; exclusion of placental and blood cells from the decidual objects; removal of one aberrant first-trimester donor; equal-cell downsampling per dataset for visualisation. ABSENT and decisive: (i) no paired/longitudinal donor sampled both before and during pregnancy; (ii) no negative control for the integration procedure - no test that anchor-based integration of two unrelated tissues fails to produce three matched clusters when no lineage relationship exists; (iii) no clustering-resolution stability analysis; (iv) no donor-genotype or any other cell-intrinsic label capable of distinguishing a carried-over cell from a newly recruited one. The authors' own third-trimester result is an internal control that failed in the direction of artefact: term decidual uNK formed only ONE cluster when analysed alone and split into three only after integration with the other datasets.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: The correspondence is circular by construction, not observed. The endometrial subsets were never independently named: Garcia-Alonso 2021, the paper Whettlock cites for "uNK1/2/3 are present in non-pregnant endometrium", states that subclustering of endometrial immune cells identified "the three uterine natural killer cell subsets WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY DEFINED IN THE EARLY PREGNANT UTERUS", annotated "by manual inspection of marker genes and interpretation of these based on the literature"; Whettlock then assigned labels with FindConservedMarkers "confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset"; and the HECA reference atlas (Mareckova 2024) projected the same labels with a CellTypist logistic-regression classifier trained on that reference. A decidual reference was therefore used to name the endometrial cells, so recovering a 1:1 endometrium-decidua match is guaranteed whether or not any endometrial cell ever becomes a decidual cell. The concrete non-carriage model that fits all the same data: uNK are re-recruited from circulating precursors after each menses and the three states are re-generated in situ by differential TGF-beta/IL-15 exposure, so endometrium and decidua contain independently generated instances of the same three attractor states rather than the same cells carried forward (Greene 2025; Strunz 2021). A second, purely technical alternative: the "three subsets" is a clustering-resolution choice, not an entity - Guo 2024, using identically processed endometrium and decidua, resolves NK1a/NK1b/NK2a/NK2b/NK3 plus three proliferating NK clusters at higher resolution, and Whettlock's own term-decidua uNK collapse to a single cluster unless integrated with the other tissues. Note for the record: no pseudotime or RNA-velocity was run on the NK compartment in the primary source, so this is not an INF_TRAJECTORY case - it is weaker still, being static cross-cohort label matching.
audit.counter_evidence: (1) Strunz B et al., "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation", Sci Transl Med 2026;18:eadp2583, PMID 41811987 - human uterus transplant and HSCT recipients; donor-vs-recipient origin of endometrial immune cells resolved GENETICALLY by SNP-based demultiplexing of scRNA-seq and by disparate HLA expression on flow: "Recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant, whereas HSCT resulted in near-complete donor-derived immune reconstitution, including formation of tissue-resident lymphocytes", with one patient's endometrium reconstituted by male-origin cells. The endometrial uNK pool is therefore continuously replaced from circulation and is not a persistent compartment that can be carried anywhere. (2) Strunz B et al., Sci Immunol 2021;6:eabb7800, PMID 33617461 - surface proteome/transcriptome plus humanised mice, human uterus transplantation and monozygotic twins; reports CONTINUOUS uNK differentiation with sequential KIR then CD39 acquisition driven by IL-15, and that "the uNK cell niche could be replenished from circulation". A continuum with sequential marker acquisition is incompatible with three discrete pre-formed subsets being carried across tissues (abstract only; science.org 403). (3) Greene M, ... Porrett PM, bioRxiv 2025.07.05.663267, PMID 40672293 - "uNKs derive from circulatory cells in the peripheral blood which immigrate into the endometrium and become resident as they reconstitute the uterine lining after menses"; divergent effector uNK subsets are produced by differences in TGF-beta responsiveness of recent immigrants, i.e. subsets are made in situ each cycle, not inherited (full text unobtainable). (4) Chiossone L, Vacca P et al., Haematologica 2014;99:448-457, PMID 24179150 - EGFP+ adoptive transfer in pregnant mice: mature peripheral NK did NOT migrate into decidua/uterus, whereas NK precursors were recruited and differentiated in situ. Direct transfer evidence for de novo generation of decidual NK (mouse; cross-species caveat). (5) Guo/Penn, Front Immunol 2024;15:1364036, PMID 38566989 - identically processed mid-secretory endometrium (n=4) and first-trimester decidua (n=4), Seurat-integrated: subsets split into NK1a/NK1b/NK2a/NK2b/NK3 plus three proliferating clusters, composition and gene expression change pre- to post-implantation, and the authors note the proliferating clusters "may represent precursor populations that give rise to particular types of NK cells". Nothing found supporting carriage: I searched specifically for paired/longitudinal same-donor endometrium-to-decidua designs and for any lineage-label or chimerism test of carriage and found none.
audit.downstream_dependency: NAMED DEPENDENCY 1: Woon EV, Greer O, Shah N, Male V, Johnson MR et al., "Uterine NK cells underexpress KIR2DL1/S1 and LILRB1 in reproductive failure", Front Immunol 2022;13:1108163, PMID 36713400 / PMC9880428. It gates uNK1-3 in NON-PREGNANT window-of-implantation endometrium from 16 women with unexplained reproductive failure vs 11 controls and concludes that reproductive failure involves "reduction in expression of uNK receptors important for interaction with HLA-C and HLA-G on EVT DURING EARLY PREGNANCY". That inference is only valid if the endometrial uNK1/2/3 measured pre-conception are the cells that will be the decidual dNK1/2/3 facing extravillous trophoblast. If instead the uNK pool is re-recruited and re-differentiated after implantation, a pre-conception biopsy cannot index decidual subset composition and the entire pre-conception "uNK subset test" rationale for recurrent miscarriage / recurrent implantation failure clinics loses its bridge. NAMED DEPENDENCY 2: Mareckova M, Garcia-Alonso L, Vento-Tormo R et al., "An integrated single-cell reference atlas of the human endometrium" (HECA), Nat Genet 2024;56:1925-1937, PMID 39198675 - hard-codes uNK1/2/3 as consensus non-pregnant endometrial cell-state labels (assigned by CellTypist logistic-regression label projection, then marker-refined) into the community reference atlas that is subsequently integrated with endometriosis GWAS data; every downstream study that maps a query dataset onto HECA inherits the decidua-derived subset identity without re-testing it. NAMED DEPENDENCY 3: the primary source's own stated purpose - Whettlock 2022 positions its cross-sectional cycle data as "a platform from which the relationship between uNK function and impaired implantation and placentation can be investigated".
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The CLASS is not overturned: Claude called it INFERENCE (shared markers) and the audit confirms INF_MARKER as the strongest class. Three substantive corrections make the claim materially weaker than that label suggests. (a) It is not an independent marker match, it is CIRCULAR. Claude's phrasing implies two separately derived label sets that happened to agree. In fact the endometrial labels were created by importing the decidual ones - Garcia-Alonso 2021 says the endometrial subsets are "the three uterine natural killer cell subsets we have previously defined in the early pregnant uterus"; Whettlock's assignment was "confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset"; HECA projected the labels with a CellTypist classifier. Agreement is an artefact of the naming pipeline, so this sits at the very bottom of INF_MARKER, not the middle. (b) The claim is not merely unsupported but AFFIRMATIVELY CONTRADICTED by evidence of a stronger class than the claim itself rests on: OBS_GENETIC chimerism in human uterus transplant/HSCT (Strunz 2026) showing the endometrial immune compartment including tissue-resident lymphocytes is replaced from circulation, and OBS_TRANSFER in mouse (Chiossone 2014) showing mature NK do not enter decidua while precursors do. Claude's call did not register that counter-evidence exists. (c) The three-subset partition is resolution-dependent, not an entity: Whettlock's own term decidua yields ONE uNK cluster alone and three only after integration with the other tissues, and Guo 2024 resolves five effector plus three proliferating clusters from the same tissues. Also corrected: the starting hint's "Wang et al. Nat Med 2020" is a misattribution for the endometrial uNK subsets (that paper exists, PMID 32929266, but describes seven epithelial/stromal cell types and no uNK1/2/3); the correct endometrial citation is Garcia-Alonso Nat Genet 2021, verified from Whettlock's reference list. One point in Claude's favour that I checked and can confirm: this is NOT a pseudotime claim - no trajectory or velocity was run on the NK compartment in any of the load-bearing papers.
audit.methods_quote: Whettlock 2022, Methods, "Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Analysis": "The four datasets were integrated based on a previously published workflow. Clusters that appeared to be non-immune cells were removed, and the remaining cells were reanalysed using the same workflow. The integrated dataset contained 2,180 cells from non-pregnant endometrium, 18,243 cells from first-trimester decidua, 3,900 from second-trimester decidua, and 6,077 from third-trimester decidua. The algorithm 'FindConservedMarkers' was used to identify the clusters uNK1, uNK2, and uNK3. This was confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset." || Whettlock 2022, Results: "Previous analysis of scRNAseq data from third-trimester decidua identified only a single cluster within the uNK population, and our reanalysis of the third-trimester dataset alone confirmed this. However, when the third-trimester data were integrated with data from the non-pregnant uterus, first- and second-trimester, the third-trimester uNK cells did form three clusters." || Garcia-Alonso 2021 (PMID 34857954), Results: "Subclustering of immune cells resolves their heterogeneity, including identification of the three uterine natural killer cell subsets we have previously defined in the early pregnant uterus"; Methods, "Annotation of scRNA-seq datasets": "Identification and labeling of the major cell types in the in vivo dataset was by manual inspection of marker genes and interpretation of these based on the literature." || Mareckova 2024 HECA (PMID 39198675), Methods: "To annotate immune cells in our datasets we first used celltypist v.0.1.9, which is a logistic regression classifier optimized by the stochastic gradient descent algorithm... After projecting labels from all three datasets, we refined the annotations using expression of bona fide markers on each cluster."
audit.notes: VERDICT: the "same subsets carried from endometrium into decidua" reading of S2 is not supported by any observation in any located primary source, and is contradicted by human transplant-chimerism and mouse transfer data. What IS supported is the much weaker statement: three transcriptionally/phenotypically analogous uNK states are detectable in both non-pregnant endometrium and decidua, in separate cross-sectional donor cohorts, with the endometrial states named after the decidual ones. The arrow in "uNK1/2/3 -> dNK1/2/3" is supplied by the reader, not by data. || Archived full texts: /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9245422.txt (Whettlock 2022, primary), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC8648563.txt (Garcia-Alonso 2021), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC11387200.txt (HECA 2024), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC10985329.txt (Guo 2024), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9880428.txt (Woon 2022), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC7612850.txt (Vento-Tormo 2018, abstract only), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_33617461.txt and S2_41811987.txt and S2_40672293.txt (abstract only), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC3943307.txt (Chiossone 2014, abstract only). || G5 compliance: every n above is donors/women; the 2,180 / 18,243 / 3,900 / 6,077 figures are cells and are recorded only as pseudoreplicate counts. || in_vivo field set to in_vivo because the load-bearing evidence is profiling of freshly isolated ex vivo tissue; the PMA/ionomycin degranulation and cytokine assays are in vitro readouts on ex vivo cells and bear on function, not on the lineage claim, so INF_INVITRO is not listed. || Uncertainty flagged honestly: Vento-Tormo 2018's original clustering methods for dNK1/2/3 could not be read (PMC record is abstract-only), so the claim that dNK1/2/3 themselves are Leiden clusters plus marker annotation is inferred from the abstract, from Whettlock's use of its "annotation" metadata column, and from Garcia-Alonso's description of them - not read from that paper's methods.
